note: Skeptic Shark, operator angle. Judged only against the five numbered North Star surfaces. A click, a cold lab, a stop, and the 0110 tailnet row are the tests — not the elegance table.

findings.criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview: started on demand (cwd = the project folder) on an OS-assigned free port that is never 8777, with its own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped when dead
findings.message: Wave 3's intent says criterion 1 is (B) and "the manager is built." The same wave's deliverable still says "Until (B) is ratified, W3.1 and its dependents spend zero." Elegance leaves W3.1 HOLD, and W4 endpoints, W5.2 lab 302, W4.2 boot reap, and W7.1 stop chip inherit that HOLD. Foreman has two sentences and they contradict. Obey the HOLD and John has no project lab, no restart of a dead one, no stop — only a classifier and some chips. Re-asking the North Star as a one-liner leaves criterion 1 unimplemented while later waves talk as if a lab exists.

findings.topic: never-blank gated on first blank click
findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> … starting or restarting the lab if needed; a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
findings.message: The interstitial is HOLD until "a recorded click that is blank or hung under a blocking 302-after-probe." Criterion 2 already forbids that click. Wave 5's own intent admits the remaining path — a spinnerless wait on the dashboard origin — is a blank page, then the deliverable still withholds the poll. Labs are started on demand, so the first click after idle is the cold path. The rebuild trigger makes John the first failing test. A lab that is "up on first probe" skips the page; the cold start, the missing-jupyter case, and the hung pid are exactly when he clicks.

findings.topic: clickable rows wired to a HOLD open
findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row (register, plan outline, files tile) opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file
findings.message: W6 KEEPs rewriting register, plan-step, and files rows to `/notebook` and painting "lab" / "notebook" / "editor" chips. W5.1 KEEPs the route. W5.2's dispatch to `ensure_lab` and the 302 to `/lab/tree/<rel>` stay HOLD with W3.1. John will see a clickable row that claims it opens where it runs. One implementation ships hrefs at a route with no lab branch (blank, 404, or hung tab). The other skips the rewrite because dispatch never shipped, so the same rows stay read-only artifacts. Either way a notebook row does not open in JupyterLab. The plan has no operator contract for what a click does while those HOLDs stand.

findings.topic: tailnet FQDN not in default allowlist
findings.section: Wave 2 / W2.1 HOLD + Wave 8 live-link fixture
findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is a http://localhost / 127.0.0.1 / <this machine's tailnet name> URL renders as a link (new window); journal 0110 — a JupyterLab or Shiny address reachable from the register and the plan without a launch page
findings.message: After the probe is HOLD, `allowed_hosts` is localhost, 127.0.0.1, `socket.gethostname()` (this machine's hostname is PUTER), and whatever someone puts in `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES`. The 0110 address is `https://gwl-server.tailb49f65.ts.net:8446/lab`. Exact hostname equality means `gwl-server` does not match that FQDN; PUTER matches neither. Wave 2's GWT only proves `http://gwl-server/shiny/app` with the env set to the short name, and still names `fake_tailscale.py` which the HOLD forbids adding. W8 then lets sign-off use "the running managed lab's URL" instead of the tailnet row, so the ship gate can go green without the motivating host ever becoming a link. Nothing in W8 sets `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES` on the live service. John clicks the register row that opened this effort and it stays text.

findings.topic: editor sign-off proves vscode:// not code -r
findings.criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`); 5 — a long .py opens in the editor (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: Criterion 3 names `code -r`. The editor page still dual-fires the seam and `location.assign(vscode://file/<abs>)`. vscode:// is HOLD until a recorded click where `code -r` failed, but Wave 8 (c) still captures a `vscode://file/` navigation request as the Playwright proof and defers the actual editor window to "eyes-on." Dual-fire can open the file twice. The operator proof is a dashboard tab that says "Opening … in the editor," not VS Code. If the HOLD is obeyed, the sign-off assertion on `vscode://` cannot pass. If it is not, the North Star editor path is still unshown.

findings.criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed — never a blank page; a stale or dead lab is restarted
findings.message: `ensure_lab` treats a live pid that fails two `/api/status` probes (1.5 s each) as dead, tree-kills it, and starts fresh. Criterion 2 restarts stale or dead labs, not slow ones. A cold JupyterLab that is still binding is killed mid-boot; the next click starts another. W5 drives ensure from the route and from `lab_ready` polls, so the first-click / double-click / poll-during-boot case is the one that hits this. The GWT only uses `FAKE_LAB_HANG` (socket accepted, never answers). Restart-on-hung becomes restart-on-not-ready-yet, which is how "come up every time" becomes "never stays up."

findings.criterion: 3 — a .py or .R row that is short (≤ 120 lines) or marked as a notebook (`# %%` cells, or `# notebook` in its first lines) is converted once … and opened in JupyterLab; the row says which ("notebook" / "editor")
findings.message: Criterion 3 scopes "first lines" to the `# notebook` marker only. `# %%` cells are a mark anywhere. `open_kind` only scans `# %%` inside the 121-line cap, so a 400-line percent-script whose first `# %%` sits on line 122 is `editor`, the chip says "editor", and `code -r` opens it. The GWT proves the opposite case (`# %%` on line 3 of a 400-line file). John clicking a VS Code-style notebook that starts after a long import block does not get a notebook. The row lies about where that file runs.

findings.topic: mixed Where cell path vs URL
findings.criterion: 3 — code rows open where they run; 4 — a Where cell that is a localhost / 127.0.0.1 / tailnet-name URL renders as a link (new window)
findings.message: The parser says a cell with both a path and a URL "keeps the path as the open target." `delivRow` takes `if (it.url)` first and never rewrites that row to `/notebook`. If `url` is still set, John clicks a `.py` and lands on the live URL. If `url` is cleared because a path exists, a register row that still has the 0110 launch-page path plus the real lab/Shiny address keeps opening the launch page — the gap this criterion exists to close. One cell cannot obey both sentences. The click is unspecified.

findings.topic: cold-start sign-off asserts lab URL on first popup
findings.criterion: 5 — on a real project, a .ipynb row opens the lab with the file selected (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: Sign-off Given is "no lab running." Wave 5 then answers that click with a 200 interstitial on the dashboard origin whose URL is `/notebook/…`, and only later sets `window.location` to `/lab/tree/…`. Wave 8 (a) asserts the popup URL contains `/lab/tree/signoff/hello.ipynb` with no wait through `lab_ready`. On the stated cold path that assertion is false at first paint. If W5.3 HOLD also stands, there is no interstitial either — Playwright is then staring at the blank click criterion 2 forbids. Criterion 5 is not met by a screenshot of a spinnerless `/notebook` tab.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb in the register, under its step in the plan, or in the files tile opens … at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel>
findings.message: Register and plan-step rows pass `path` plus `dir=<effort-rel>`. The files tile is specified as `dir=''` and "project-relative path," and the gate only asserts that `openProducedFile` / `renderFiles` contain a `/notebook` `window.open` string. Wave 8 never clicks a files-tile row. If the files payload is effort-relative (a produced `hello.ipynb` under the campaign dir), `/notebook` joins it at the project root, the route 404s with no echo, and the third named surface is a blank tab. Criterion 2 lists that surface as equal to the register.

findings.topic: missing ir kernel has no honest state
findings.criterion: 3 — kernel python3 or ir; Statement — short code as a Jupyter notebook in the project's own JupyterLab (Python and R kernels)
findings.message: Missing jupyter is an honest reason on the click. Missing `ir` is not. `to_notebook` still stamps `.R` with kernelspec `ir`. Wave 8 treats IRkernel as a host inventory fact and screenshots the stamp. Execution-on-open is a non-goal; shipping an R kernel in the lab is not. John clicking a short `.R` still gets a sibling notebook whose kernel the lab may not have, with no reason on the page and a "notebook" chip that says it runs.

The locked words are "notebook" and "editor." The chip prints `open_kind.kind`, so a `.ipynb` row says "lab." An operator reading the row for where it runs has to know that "lab" means the notebook. Harmless if the click works; it is not the vocabulary the criterion named.
